title_as_printed: Measured and calculated methane water content in the presence of hydrates/water at different conditions
pressure_note: equilibrium cell pressure (strain gauge transducer checked with a dead weight tester); absolute or gauge not stated

T.constant: set by group_rows (block label rows '15 C', '5 C', ...)

value.what: water content of the methane-rich gas phase, printed in 'ppm' (mole/volume/mass basis not stated in this table; see notes)

uncertainty.constant: +-1 % of reading or 4 ppm, whichever is greater (text p.148)

composition.other_species: distilled water (aqueous or hydrate phase present)

skip_rows.reason: temperature block label rows and 'AAD %' summary rows

row_regime_overrides.reason: Equilibrium state column 'VHE' (methane in equilibrium with hydrate; assignment by the authors from a CALCULATED hydrate dissociation pressure)

conversion_needs: ppm to mole fraction (x1e-6) once the ppm basis is settled
notes: Method: low-temperature rig (T <= 25 C): rocking titanium equilibrium cell; gas sampled through a heated line (100 C) to a Yokogawa TDLAS (tunable diode laser absorption spectrometer, operated at 50 C and 0.34 barg, range to 3000 ppm, stated accuracy +-1 % of reading). The table header says only 'ppm'. Tables 4.4-4.6 (same rig, same TDLAS) label the quantity 'y_w - ppm' and Table 4.7 (GC) 'y_w - ppmV', so a mole (volume) basis is likely, but this table does not state it. Temperature is printed only in the grey block rows (filled by group_rows). '101' bar printed without decimals. VLE rows below 0 C: [22] (authors call these VLE; at -5 C the condensed water phase would be ice or supercooled water; note below_273K). All rows below 273.15 K are kept (builder tags them). 2026-10-11 coordinator: 'ppm' read as ppm by mole. Check against other laboratories in the database at the same T and P (interpolated in ln P): Table 4.13 CO2 over water, 100 and 150 C, 16-138 bar: ratio Teymouri/others 0.79-0.99 (Hou 2013b, Zawisza 1981, Caumon 2016, Tabasinejad 2011, King 1971); a mass basis would make the mole fractions 2.44 times larger (ratio about 2-2.4). Table 4.2 CH4 over water, 5 and 15 C: ratio 0.91-1.12 against Chapoy 2003/2005. Same instruments as Tables 4.4-4.7, printed 'y_w - ppm' and 'ppmV'.
